description: Atomic facts on nitrification capacity and basil N uptake, added 2026-11-25. Candidates until Ajit approves them. Reliability recorded per AGENTS.md 6A.

facts.statement: In UVI-style raft aquaponics, the raft can treat the waste of about 180 g of fish feed per m2 of grow area per day, if solids are removed before the raft.

context.condition: solids removed upstream of the raft

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: source level E4; direct_quote; context partial
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Extension fact sheet by UVI's lead researcher. It does not say at what TAN level this applies, or whether plant ammonium uptake is included. Cross-check: Consistent with UVI's statement that the raft gives adequate biofiltration at the design feed ratio; about 10x higher per m2 than trickling-filter and RBC biofilm rates, which are not directly comparable.
review_metadata.reviewed_from_file: web reads 2026-11-25 (see data/knowledge/models/nitrification_models.json and basil.json for URLs)

facts.statement: Biofilter nitrification rate rises roughly in step with TAN below about 2 mg/L and stops rising above about 3 to 4 mg/L.

facts.statement: Nitrification works best from pH 7.0 up (more efficient in the high 8s) and practically stops below pH 6.0.

review_metadata.confidence_reason: SRAC 454 and the UVI system page agree on the endpoints; matches existing canon (inhibited at or below pH 6.0).

facts.statement: Temperature affects fixed-film nitrification less than the Arrhenius equation predicts: at 20 C the rate rises about 4.3 percent per C when TAN-limited and about 1.1 percent per C when oxygen-limited.
